block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Neither off-plan nor ready property is automatically better for every buyer. For visa-focused buyers, compare price, payment timing, financing, construction risk, handover certainty, immediate use or rent and visibility over the finished property. Choose the route whose trade-offs best match the buyer’s timeline, cash flow and tolerance for uncertainty.

items.answer: Neither off-plan nor ready property is automatically better for every buyer. For visa-focused buyers, set the expected off-plan handover against the immediate usability of ready property and the buyer's actual move-in or income timeline.
items.question: Which is better: off-plan or ready property?

items.answer: Off-plan and ready property solve different buyer needs, so neither is universally better. Model deposits, instalments, financing and completion payments for both routes instead of comparing only the initial purchase price.
items.question: How do I compare off-plan and ready property?

items.answer: Off-plan and ready property offer different trade-offs rather than a universally better choice. Account for construction, delivery and specification risk in off-plan while checking condition, refurbishment and existing-building risks in ready property.
items.question: How do off-plan and ready property compare?

items.answer: The best developer questions test the facts behind price, delivery and the contract. Understand defect handling, warranties, building management and owner support because developer quality continues to matter after completion.
items.question: What questions should I ask the developer?

items.answer: Handover delay risk is the possibility that completion takes longer than the buyer expects. A small delay would create major practical or financial problems for the buyer. Verify current project status before relying on a fixed move-in, rental or completion date.
